points.resolution_note: One token was wrong, in exactly one variant. to-nai-stem is the な-inclusive stem (書く -> 書かな, 食べる -> 食べな), so appending "ないまま" doubles the な and yields 書かなないまま / 食べなないまま. The token must be "いまま". This is not a judgement call: the same grammar point is encoded at N3 as gram:n3-mama with [to-nai-stem] + "いまま" and the identical example 食べないまま, so the two records now agree and only the N4 one was wrong. The other four variants were re-executed against the full test set and every output is grammatical and matches the record's own formation text (verbo no passado simples -> 立ったまま; adjetivo-い -> 安いまま; adjetivo-な + な -> 静かなまま; substantivo + の -> 昔のまま), so they are re-emitted unchanged, including their exact step shapes, which are identical to gram:n3-mama's. nuance_tags [continuation] and usage_contexts [spoken, written] are untouched — no finding touched them and both are grounded in the record.

points.resolution_note: The restriction is real and the closed base enum cannot carry it. The record's formation states the host type outright — "número + contador + おきに" — and every instance it carries is a quantity phrase: 10分おきに, 1メートルおきに, 1日おきに. The base enum offers verb / i-adjective / na-adjective / noun / clause / any, and none of them means "numeral + counter". Declaring base "noun" is what the withheld variant did, and a consumer expanding it over the vocab registry produces *学生おきに, *本おきに, *猫おきに — the `example` field pins 10分おきに but example is documentation, not a constraint. Narrowing the base is not available, splitting into variants does not help (every split still lands on `noun`), and inventing a base value is forbidden. So no variant is emitted. Note this is a schema-level gap rather than a defect in this record: the record itself is precise and its nuance_tags [] is honest (the enum has no interval/frequency member), and gram:gp-70 (ごとに) and gram:gp-68 (ごろ) have the same host type. Nothing else in the record is changed.
points.steps_unavailable: おきに attaches to a quantity expression (numeral + counter), not to a noun: the record's own formation says "número + contador + おきに" (10分おきに, 1メートルおきに, 1日おきに, 一人おきに). The closed base enum has no quantity/counter member, and the only base that would accept these hosts, `noun`, also accepts every ordinary noun in the vocab registry, licensing *学生おきに and *本おきに — precisely the error the point exists to prevent. No safe variant can be expressed; the counter phrase must be built by the caller and おきに appended to it.

points.resolution_note: Six of the eight withheld variants are productive and execute clean; the two that were dropped both encoded a LEXICAL exception as a class-wide surface rule. Variant 7 ({i-adjective, replace-ending いい→よさそう}) fires on any adjective whose surface merely ends in いい, so かわいい — an i_adj in this corpus's own N5 vocab — yields *かわよさそうな, when the general variant already gives the correct かわいそうな. Variant 8 ({i-adjective, replace-ending ない→なさそう}) mis-targets its own case: the record's ない is the negative auxiliary (its Exceções line sits beside いい→よさそう, and the whole point is stem-based 様態 そう), so as an i-adjective ending-match it never reaches the verb negative it exists for and instead fires on lexical -ない adjectives, where 汚い yields *きたなさそうな instead of 汚そう. Both are dropped. In their place the negative IS given its own variant, because it is expressible: to-nai-stem is the な-inclusive stem, so [verb, to-nai-stem] + "さそうな" derives exactly what the record states (ない → なさそう) — 降る -> 降らなさそうな, 書く -> 書かなさそうな — with the な/に pair the record defines as fully general over the そう stem ("+ な antes de substantivo, + に antes de verbo"). Dropping variant 8 also repairs 汚い, which now takes the general rule and gives 汚そうな. What remains unencodable is the いい exception itself, recorded in steps_unavailable. Noun is correctly still not claimed. nuance_tags [conjecture] and usage_contexts [spoken, written, casual-friends] are untouched.
points.steps_unavailable: Two things the emitted variants deliberately do not cover. (1) いい → よさそう. It is a lexeme-scoped exception and the variant schema has only base/steps/example — no lexical scope. It cannot be rescued by a surface ending-match either: the adjectives that need it are the ones whose final element IS the lexeme いい (いい → よさそう, 気持ちいい → 気持ちよさそう, かっこいい → かっこよさそう), and they are indistinguishable by surface ending from かわいい, whose correct form かわいそう comes from the general い→そう variant. So the general i-adjective variant emitted here must not be applied to that lexeme set: on いい it would produce *いそう. (2) The negative of an i-adjective (高くない → 高くなさそう). The op enum has no negative-adjective step, and encoding it as replace-ending い→くなさそう would fire on いい as well (*いくなさそう). Only the verb negative is encoded, via to-nai-stem + さそう.

points.resolution_note: The defect here is not in the steps. Both checkers raised the same omission: variant 5 emits 〜てくださる, which the record's own formation labels "Versão respeitosa, quando o favor vem de um superior" — くださる is 尊敬語, the closed enum carries an exact member for it, and nuance_tags was [request] alone. Fixed by adding "honorific", which is what the sibling gram:o-kudasai-2 already carries for the same くださる family. The five variants were re-executed against the full verb set and every output is grammatical and matches the record's own conjugation list (くれます polido, くれた passado, くれない negativo, くださる respeitosa), so they are re-emitted unchanged — this is a tag repair, not a step rewrite. Two things I did NOT do. The second checker also observed that "request" is the record's secondary sense (drawn from the one aside 〜てくれない？) while its primary content is direction of benefit and gratitude; that primary sense has no member in the closed nuance enum, so it cannot be tagged and "request" stays, since it is genuinely grounded. And I did not add "politeness" for くれます: there the ます form is listed as an ordinary conjugation slot available to any verb, not as a register choice, and usage_contexts carries no business/formal context — unlike gram:te-morau, where the respectful set is framed as a register choice. usage_contexts [spoken, written] unchanged.
